meta.dataset: CET / Horton Electrical - municipal wastewater (WPCF/WWTF) target accounts, CT-MA-RI
meta.method: The facility universe comes from EPA ECHO's CWA REST API (SIC 4952 sewerage, NPDES majors in CT/MA/RI), plus MA POTW General Permit (MAG59/MAG58) plants, CT minor plants with funded projects, and a few Cape Cod/Nantucket groundwater-permit plants with large SRF projects. ECHO supplies the permit ID, design flow and facility coordinates. Project, stage and value data come from three state lists, matched by NPDES ID or municipality: CT DEEP's FINAL Clean Water Fund Priority List FY2026-27 (issued 2026-07-22), the MassDEP/Mass Clean Water Trust 2026 Final CWSRF IUP (Tables 1-4), and the RIDEM/RIIB SFY2027 CWSRF draft IUP/PPL (June 2026). Energy signals come from those lists (green-reserve and energy flags) and from utility renewable-energy pages (NBC, GLSD, MWRA). horton_fit (0-98) is a transparent heuristic: state base (CT 30 / MA 26 / RI 22), +4 for MA counties near CET's Worcester/Taunton offices, design-flow band (+3 to +20), project class (plant funded 32, plant requested 24, pump station funded 22, pump station requested 16, planning 10, collection 6, none 0), +8 for electrical/aeration/generator/resiliency/plant-upgrade keywords, +2 to +6 for pipeline value, and +2 for an energy signal. cross_sell is rule-based: solar if the plant is ≥1 MGD or solar/renewable is mentioned and there is no large existing on-site renewable; storage if the plant is ≥10 MGD or has existing renewables/cogen/resiliency work; generator for pump-station, resiliency, electrical or coastal sites; efficiency for aeration/blower/UV/HVAC work or plants ≥1 MGD; ev for plants ≥20 MGD.
sources_summary: EPA ECHO CWA REST services (echodata.epa.gov) - NPDES facility search CT/MA/RI
CT DEEP Clean Water Fund Final Priority List FY2026-2027 (portal.ct.gov/deep) + draft list 12/29/2025
MassDEP / Massachusetts Clean Water Trust - 2026 Final CWSRF Intended Use Plan (mass.gov)
RIDEM / RI Infrastructure Bank - SFY2027 CWSRF Intended Use Plan & draft PPL (dem.ri.gov); SFY2026 IUP (riib.org)
Narragansett Bay Commission renewable energy page (narrabay.com)
Greater Lawrence Sanitary District Project Net-Zero (glsd.org)
caveats: The RI project list is the June 2026 DRAFT SFY2027 IUP/PPL. Only Table 2 "Project Funding List" items are proposed for funding; other PPL rows are ranked needs.

CT Table 3 items are requests eligible for first-come reserves; only Table 2 / Category I items are on the fundable list. Dollar figures are the applicant cost estimates in the lists, not contract awards.

project_value_usd is the primary (first-listed) project total; pipeline_value_usd sums every listed facility-related item (some are collection-system or tributary-town projects). MA figures are total project cost; the 2026 IUP offer can be smaller (noted per project).

In ECHO, many MA plants moved from individual permits to the MA POTW General Permit (MAG590000/MAG580000), which carries no design flow. For those, design_flow_mgd comes from the plant's prior (terminated) individual ECHO record, and design_flow_source says so. Amesbury's prior value (24 MGD) looked anomalous and was set to null.
ECHO NPDES status is often "Admin Continued"/"Expired" for CT/MA permits. That reflects EPA/state backlog, not plant closure.
Coordinates: ECHO/FRS facility coordinates are labeled 'address'. The six Cape Cod/Nantucket groundwater-permit plants and Coventry CT use ZIP (ZCTA) centroids, labeled 'city'.
NBC funding-list rows all cite permit RI0100315. Bucklin Point (BPWWTF) projects were re-mapped to RI0100072 by project name.
The operator field shows the owner/authority. Contract O&M operators were not verified.
The Middletown CT WPCF (terminated permit; flows diverted to Mattabassett) and the Boston/Cambridge/Somerville/Chelsea CSO-only permits were excluded.

horton_fit and cross_sell are heuristic prioritization aids, not validated win probabilities. Horton's existing client and incumbency relationships were not researched: the web-search budget ran out and ZoomInfo was not used.
The Plainfield CT secondary-clarifier request names only the town. It was attached to Plainfield North WPCF (the major permit).

scoring_fields.project_class: plant_funded | plant_requested | ps_funded | ps_requested | planning | collection | none

priority_top_15.rationale: GNHWPCA's 40 MGD East Shore plant has an $82M wet-weather/odor-control upgrade on CT's FY27 fundable list, and a separate $19.2M process-air-compressor request, in Horton's home state.
MDC's Hartford WPCF is CT's largest plant (60 MGD). It has $24.3M of sludge screening and equalization work fundable in FY26-27, plus $31.6M in Island Road and Hog Brook pump-station requests.

Norwalk has a $26M final-settling-tank upgrade fundable in FY27 and a $48M green aeration-system request. Aeration is the plant's biggest energy load, which makes it a natural Horton electrical + NuWave efficiency pairing.

MWRA Deer Island is carrying a $289M Clarifier #2 project in the 2026 IUP. The plant already self-generates 26% of its electricity, so the angle is electrical subcontracting plus storage/efficiency, not solar.

Bridgeport West Side has CT's largest program: a $350M phased WPCF upgrade ($125M FY26 + $125M FY27 fundable) on top of a $30M Phase 1. A general contractor will likely lead it, so the target is the electrical/I&C subcontract.

Danbury pairs a fundable digester upgrade with requests for $11.3M of WWTP solar, $11.4M of cogeneration, a generator upgrade, switchgear relocation and pump-station SCADA/generators. That is the strongest single Horton + NuWave cross-sell bundle on the list.
Mattabassett District's 20 MGD regional plant in Cromwell has fundable green resiliency/aeration and odor-control upgrades, which bring blower, VFD and standby-power scope.

NBC Field's Point has a $12.2M WWTF Electrical Improvements project on RI's SFY27 funding list, plus $38.5M of plant improvements and a $34.5M Ernest St pump station. Wind is already on site, so pitch storage and efficiency.
Haverhill's $66.5M WWTF and South Mill St pump-station upgrade was offered $50M in MA's 2026 IUP. It is a funded, near-term construction project within reach of CET's Massachusetts base.
Bristol's $4.65M aeration-blowers upgrade is fundable in FY27 under the Green Project Reserve. It is a quick-win electrical/VFD and energy-efficiency scope.

NBC Bucklin Point has $60.3M of CSO-driven clarifiers/flow splitters, $24.3M of UV disinfection and $14.5M of digestion improvements, all electrical-heavy scopes. A biogas CHP plant is already operating there.
Derby's $60M full WPCF upgrade with nutrient removal is fundable in FY27. At 3.5 MGD the plant is small enough for Horton to be the prime electrical contractor on the complete plant package.
Waterbury's 27 MGD plant has requested a $10M green aeration-tank blower replacement, which pairs motor/VFD electrical work with measurable energy savings.

Hull's $9.63M clarifier, grit and building upgrade is the top-ranked project in MA's 2026 IUP (rating 556) and is flagged as having energy-efficiency/green components. The coastal site also favors resiliency generators.
New Bedford's 30 MGD plant has an $11.25M WWTP-improvements project on the 2026 PPL and $22.6M of IUP-funded collection work, all within easy reach of CET's Taunton office.
